userestrict.head: Conditions Governing Use
userestrict.p: Ford Foundation has title, copyright and literary rights in the collection, in so far as it holds them.

The Rockefeller Archive Center has authority to grant permission to cite and publish material from the collection. Permission to publish extensive excerpts, or material in its entirety, will be referred to the Ford Foundation.

acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: Ford Foundation archive was deposited at the RAC in 2011. Ford Foundation records, correspondence, reports, program files, and officers' papers were transferred to and accessioned by the RAC beginning in 2011. Accessions continue as necessary.
This material was transferred to the RAC as part of a larger accession in 2021. This accession was ingested by the RAC as Accession 2021:067.

bioghist.head: Biographical / Historical
bioghist.p: The Ford Foundation opened its office in Nairobi, Kenya in 1963. Since that time, it has primarily overseen the Foundation's grant programming for the Eastern Africa region, including the countries of Kenya, Tanzania, and Uganda.

Over the years, the program focus of the Nairobi Office has shifted with changes in priorities and larger Foundation program structuring. Historically, the Nairobi Office and the Foundation's Eastern Africa programming have been part of the Foundation's larger Africa and Middle East program. When it opened, the Nairobi Office served both the Eastern and Central Africa regions. From the early 1970s to 1996, the Nairobi Office was organized as the Office for Eastern and Southern Africa.

While the Nairobi Office was the Office for Eastern and Southern Africa, it had a suboffice in Harare, Zimbabwe between 1989 and 1996 and conducted programming for Zimbabwe, Angola, and Mozambique. The Harare office closed in 1996, and the Foundation's offices in Johannesburg, South Africa and Windhoek, Namibia took responsibility for the Foundation's programming for the Southern Africa region.

Throughout its history, the Nairobi Office has managed grants for supporting civil society, higher education, human rights and social justice, democracy and law, reproductive health, economic development, and youth development among other areas.
Representatives for Eastern Africa have included: Francis Sutton, John Robin, David Anderson, David Smock, Goran Hyden, William Saint Jr., Charles Bailey, Katharine Pearson, Omotade Aina.

arrangement.head: Arrangement
arrangement.p: The collection is comprised of three series. Original order was maintained as much as possible.
The collections arrangement is as follows:
Series 3. Mary Ann Burris office files, 1994-2004

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: The collection contains the office files of the Ford Foundation's East Africa Regional Office based in Nairobi, Kenya. The Foundation's East Africa program has historically been part of its larger Africa and Middle East Program. It was formerly directly tied with the Foundation's programming for Southern Africa as the Office for Eastern and Southern Africa. Collection materials reflect this history, so users will find content pertaining to programming for East African countries like Kenya, Uganda, and Tanzania as well as content pertaining to Southern African countries like Zimbabwe, Angola, and Mozambique.

The collection is made up of three series. The first series contains subject files that document the Nairobi Office's program activities between the late 1980s and early 2000s. They include materials regarding support for Southern African countries up until 1996 when the Nairobi Office moved from being the Office for Eastern and Southern Africa to the Office for Eastern Africa.

The second series contains chronology files consisting of chronologically arranged correspondence from Nairobi Office program staff, and the third series contains the office files of Nairobi Program Officer Mary Ann Burris.

At this time, the collection contains materials from just a small part of the Nairobi Office's history. Records in the collection show that within that timeframe (late 1980s to early 2000s), the Nairobi Office was active in the areas of civil society, community development, higher education, economic development, youth development, human rights, democracy, law, the environment, and reproductive health. The Nairobi Office pursued these activities in Kenya and Eastern Africa and also collaborated with the other Ford Foundation Africa regional offices in Johannesburg, Lagos, and Cairo for larger African initiatives.
In addition to the already described material formats, the collection includes reports, meeting materials, invoices, articles, notes, and several photographs.

did.unittitle: Subject files

physdesc.extent: 15.5 document boxes: 10 letter boxes and 5.5 legal boxes

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains subject files created and maintained by the Ford Foundation's Nairobi, Kenya Office between the late 1980s and the early 2000s.

Materials in the earlier part of the series originate from when the Nairobi Office served as the Foundation's Office for Eastern and Southern Africa and maintained a suboffice in Harare, Zimbabwe. Some of these materials appear to have been originally created by that suboffice and may have been transferred to Nairobi during the course of the Office for Eastern and Southern Africa's activities or after the closure of the Harare Office in 1996 and the program restructuring that made the Nairobi Office the Office for Eastern Africa. These materials principally concern programming in the countries of Angola and Mozambique.

Other materials in the series document the Nairobi Office's program interests for Kenya and Eastern Africa throughout the 1990s into the early 2000s. Files show the Office's focus on the Africa Philanthropy Initiative, the Kenya Community Development Foundation (KCDF), and the Higher Education in Africa Initiative, They highlight the work of Elkanah Odembo (Consultant for the Africa Philanthropy Initiative), Katharine Pearson (Representative for Eastern Africa), and Anne-Marea Griffin (Program Consultant) among other Nairobi Office staff.
Materials in the series include correspondence, notes, reports, meeting materials, and a few photographs.

Chronology files

physdesc.extent: 2 document boxes: 1.5 letter boxes and .5 legal box

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains chronology files created and maintained by the Ford Foundation's Nairobi, Kenya Office. Chronology files are comprised of chronologically arranged outgoing correspondence. So far, the series includes a limited range of these files from the late 1980s and 1990s.

Several of the chronology files contain the correspondence of specific Nairobi Program Officers. For those files, the Program Officer's name is included in the file title. Other files are comprised of correspondence from a number of different Program Officers and other Nairobi Office staff members.

Correspondence in the series document program interests of the Nairobi Office including disaster preparedness and management, human rights, social justice, law, refugees, democracy, and higher education throughout Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, and other parts of Africa. Correspondents include grantees, individuals and organizations seeking foundation assistance, and other Ford Foundation staff.

did.unittitle: Mary Ann Burris office files

physdesc.extent: 4.5 document boxes: 3.5 letter boxes and 1 1/2 letter box

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This series contains the office files Mary Ann Burris created and maintained when she served as a Program Officer in the Ford Foundation's Nairobi, Kenya Office between 1995 and 2002.

The files include correspondence, meeting materials, reports, invoices, articles, publications, and photographs that document Burris' work managing the Foundation's programming for economic development, reproductive health, youth development, the environment, and civil society in Kenya and East Africa. The Nairobi Office's work on the East Africa Youth Development Initiative (FAP 09890022) is documented within a few different files.
